rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING THE DANGEROUS DRUGS ACT OF 2001 REPEALING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6425, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: "Dangerous Drugs Act of 2001." This bill seeks to STRENGTHEN the existing law on Drugs, RA No. 6425, with the following AMENDMENTS: (1) Single definition of "dangerous drugs", covering both prohibited and regulated drugs;  (2) INCREASED penalties and fines for unlawful importation; illegal possession; (3) Increase in board membership; (4) Mandatory drug testing for applicants of driver's license permit to carry firearm, etc.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04433

rows.author: D055
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8042, ENTITLED `AN ACT TO INSTITUTE THE POLICIES OF OVERSEAS EMPLOYMENT AND ESTABLISH A HIGHER STANDARD OF PROTECTION AND PROMOTION OF THE WELFARE OF MIGRANT WORKERS, THEIR FAMILIES AND OVERSEAS FILIPINOS IN DISTRESS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to ensure FULL PROTECTION and PROMOTION of the RIGHTS and WELFARE of OVERSEAS FILIPINO WORKERS. The following issues are, therefore, sought to be addressed through this proposed measure:  (1) Abandon the present policy of deregulating the overseas labor industry and reassert the government's primary role in the protection and promotion of OFWs rights and welfare. (2) Address the problems of trafficking to women and minors for commercial sex purposes and forced labor. (3) Implement a comprehensive program to support migrant families. (4) Implement the needs and welfare of our sea-based OFWs. (5) Incorporate the needs and welfare of our sea-based OFWs.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-10-25

rows.abstract: It is the policy of the State to establish and maintain a complete, adequate, and consolidated National Identification System (National ID) relevant to the goal of improved public administration. To achieve this, the government shall ensure that theNational Identification System shall aid the following objectives: (1) To streamline and economize the bureaucracy by consolidation of the ID sysatems present with the National ID system; (2) To facilitate and expedite statistical data gathering bypertinent government institutions in aid of planning activities; and (3) To provide Filipino citizens with a simple and effective identification system to conduct transactions.

rows.author: C091
rows.title_full: AN ACT FIXING THE RETIREMENT AGE OF THE UNIFORMED PERSONNEL OF THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The age of compulsory retirement of the members of the PNP from the rank of Police Officer 1 up to the rank of Senior Police Officer IV is hereby fixed at 56 years.  PNP officers from the rank of Inspector to the rank of Chief Superintendent shall be compulsory retired at the age of 58 years; Provided, That a Director, a Deputy Director General and a Director General shall each be granted another year of service before retirement.> The premature retirement under existing laws of the uniformed personnel of the Philippine National Police (PNP), especially those in the upper echelons of the organization, deprives the people, of the services of thos who have the skills, knowledge and training as professional police officers.

rows.author: C005
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING THE DANGEROUS DRUGS ACT OF 2001 REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6425, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: Rationale: The illegal drug trade had been a perennial problem in our country for quite a time now. Many stories have been printed in newspapers and reported in broadcast media about self-confessed drug users whose lives were totally destroyed by illegal substances. We have also heard and witnessed how illegal drugs have destroyed families and shattered dreams of so many individuals.> This bill therefore aims to put an end to all forms of drug abuse and institute measureas that will curb drug-related activities in the country. It also aims to provide a program for rehabilitation and treatment of drug dependents and to encourage them to once again become responsible and productive citizens of our society.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04433

rows.author: C066
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A SEPARATE COMPENSATION SCHEME FOR LAWYER POSITIONS IN THE OFFICE OF THE SECRETARY OF JUSTICE, DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE, THEREBY EXEMPTING THE SAID POSITIONS FROM REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6758, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE SALARY STANDARDIZATIONLAW
rows.abstract: Any provisions of law to the contrary notwithstanding , all lawyer positions under the Office of the Secretary of Justice, which shall include but not limited to the Secretary, Undersecretarie s, Assistant Secretaries, members of the National Prosecution Service and members of the Legal Staff shall be exempt from the coverage of the Salary Standardization Law Republic Act No. 6758.> The Secretary of Justice is hereby authorized to prepare a compensation structure for said lawyer positions whichshall be based on a comprehensive job analysis and audit of actual duties and responsibilitie s and shall be comparable with the prevailing compensation plan in practice of the legal profession in the private sector. Such compensation plan shall besubject to the approval by the President.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06654

rows.abstract: "National Prosecution Service Act of 2001." Rationale: Government prosecutors are in the forefront of the fight against criminality. They have the principal task of determining the existence of probable cause and providing the commission of crime beyond reasonable doubt. They perform work akin to judges of the courts. > This bill seeks to address the need for the effective delivery of prosecutorial services nationwide with amendatory provisions, such as on: (1) Organization and structure of theNational Prosecution Service; (2) Qualification of prosecution Officers and Compensation; (3) Functions of the Regional State Prosecution Officers; as well as of the provincial, city prosecutor, etc.

rows.author: B024
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING THE ABACA AS THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL FIBER
rows.abstract: Rationale: Abaca, scientifically known as Musa Textilis Nee, is endemic to the Philippines whose warm, wet climate and volcanic soild are particularly suited to its cultivation. The crop has been grown in the Philippines for centuries and was knownto the Filipinos long before the Spanish occuption. Abaca was one of only two export commodities which contributed to an sustained the expansion of the Philippine economy in the nineteenth century, the other being sugar.> Philippine abaca is part ofour history and cultural heritage. It has sustained the domestic economy during the struggle years of our country and eventually has helped make the Philippines known in the international market. Its potential contribution in the conversion of forestt resources cannot be underestimated. There is no other natural fiber in the world today that could come close to the superior and versatile qualities of the abaca, and it is with pride that we should recognize and uphold the importance of this truly

rows.title_full: AN ACT PUNISHING ANY PERSON OR ENTITY CAUSING THE CONSTRUCTION OF ANY MARKET STALL OR STRUCTURE THAT BLOCKS OR OBSTRUCTS ANY PART OF A PUBLIC ROAD, BOULEVARD, AVENUE, HIGHWAY OR SIDEWALK, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Any person or juridical entity constructing any permanent, temporary or makeshift stall or structure along any public road, highway or sidewalk shall be imposed the penalty of not more than six months of imprisonment or a fine of not less than FiveThousand Pesos (P5,000.00) but not more than Fifty Thousand Pesos (P50,000.00), or both, at the discretation of the court. Provided that if the offender is a corporation, partnership, association or other judicial entity causing such construction. Provided further that any form of structure situated along such public road, highway or sidewalk shall be subjected to demolition and removal.

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS TO CONDUCT A QUARTERLY BREAST CANCER DETECTION PROGRAM
rows.abstract: The Local Government Units are hereby directed, thru its local health officers and in close coordination with the Deaprtment of Health, to hold a quarterly manual or mammogram breast cancer screening program. The Program will utilize the services ofthe Barangay/Munici pal/City/Provin cial Health Workers in identifying breast cancer cases and positive cases will be immediately referred to public health hospitals for treatment, management and rehabilitation. The Health Workers concerned shall then maintain case records on each individual found positive of breast cancer.

rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE CAPABILITY OF THE BUREAU OF FOOD AND DRUGS (BFAD) BY ESTABLISHING ADEQUATE TESTING LABORATORIES AND REGIONAL FIELD OFFICES, UPGRADING ITS EQUIPMENT, CREATION OF A DRUG ENFORCEMENT UNIT UNDER ITS OPERATIONAL AND ADMINISTRATIVE CONTROL, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: "BFAD Empowerment Act of 2001". Rationale: There is a need to TRANSFORM BFAD into a more and credible regulatory agency, and to borrow the words of the UP Policy Review Team, one whose integrity and credibility are above reproach and if possible, beyond any reasonable doubt. To achieve this, it is vital, among other things not only to provide adequate funding for the agency but more importantly, introduce major administrative reforms in BFAD to strengthen the capability of BFAD's regulatory functions of licensing, registration and monitoring, and more spefically in the following aspects: (1) Human resources in the field; (2) Augmentation of existing laboratories and upgrading their equipment; (3) Operational budget; and (4) Creation of a ddrug enforcement unit under its operational and administrative control.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05497

rows.author: B024
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING FIRST CLASS COASTAL MUNICIPALITIES AND ALL COASTAL CITIES AND PROVINCES TO HAVE A FISHERIES OFFICER
rows.abstract: Rationale: The vastness of the Philippine maritime zone and its rich resources dictate that we should have a marine-based economy. Our aquatic territory exceeding 220 million hectares is more than seven (7) times our land territory which is only 30million hectares. Being on archipelago of more than seven thousand islands, the Philippines should have been the center of the fishing industry in Asia, if not of the world.> This bill seeks to attune the policy of the State to our nature as an archipelago be encouraging our people to invest in fisheries. It will provide support to the fishery sector by requiring the appointment of a fisheries officer in all first class coastal municipalities and in all coastal cities and provinces.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-11-19

rows.author: C069
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 12 AND 13 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7662, ENTITLED `AN ACT PROVIDING FOR REFORMS IN LEGAL EDUCATION, CREATING FOR THE PURPOSE A LEGAL EDUCATION BOARD AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Ra No. 7662 was enacted in 1993 primarily to give flesh to the declared State policy to uplift the standards of legal education. And yet, a reading of the law would reveal certain provisions that go beyond the ambit of education of aspiring lawyers and into the sphere of education of persons duly licensed to practice the law profession. These provisions do not only expand the purpose of the law - these also impinge on matters that might render their implementation constitutionaly infirm. > Events have likewise overtaken the implementation of the law. However, for a smooth implementation of the law, its objectionable provisions must be corrected. Immediate amendment of Republic Act No. 7662 bodes well for the attainment of the aiims for which it was enacted.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-11-19

rows.author: D075
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING AN EMERGENCY MEASURE TO ALLEVIATE THE PLIGHT OF COCONUT FARMERS ADVERSELY AFFECTED BY LOW PRICES OF COPRA AND OTHER COCONUT PRODUCTS, AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: In order to immediately address the abnormal price situation in the coconut industry sector brought by the worldwide glut of fats and oild in the world market, there is a need to launch an income supplment program for small coconut farmers, tillers, workers and owners-cultivat ors who comprise the overwhelming majority of the people in the coconut industry that will provide them immediate relief from adverse effects of extremely low prices of copra and husket nuts.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE, FOOD & FISHERIES since 2001-11-19
